title: Inner products, orthogonality, and least squares

runs.text: . Over C, this article uses the convention linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second.
Gram-Schmidt replaces an independent list by an orthonormal list with the same successive spans.
The normal equations make the residual b-Axhat orthogonal to the column space. If A has independent columns, the least-squares solution is unique.

items.text: Projection and orthogonality require a specified inner product; the displayed coordinate formulas use the standard Euclidean real inner product.
For complex matrices, replace transposes in the normal equations by conjugate transposes.
Gram-Schmidt requires the input list to be linearly independent; discard zero residuals only when processing a redundant spanning list.
The normal equations can have many solutions when A has dependent columns, although the projected vector is unique.
Normalize after subtracting all earlier projections in Gram-Schmidt.
